items.title: 67426_Hayes Pillars oral history interview
items.q: So this was the end of the Jater-Pillars band.

ctx.x: Well, everybody claimed I sounded so good the way I was playing, why change. And I noticed one day I tried to put my teeth on there, and it jarred me. It just shook my head, you know, man. And I said, 'Well, I'm just going to stick to my way of blowing my horn.' Then I found out in later years that most saxophone players who had blown that way -- the orthodox way of playing a saxophone -- their teeth -- they had worked a little curve in their teeth. A little curve in their teeth.

Just like my partner Jater-- (unintelligible) his teeth finally wore out and he had to have new teeth put in up there. And I still got my two front teeth, because I never used them that way, you know.

And -- but this is what I did. I pulled the chart out. And I looked on the chart and I didn't see a thing about do or anything like that. (Interruption) Ready? I noticed when I got home that night, as I said before, I kept fooling with my horn, blowing, blowing, blowing, until I was able to run the C scale. It sound terrible, but it sound good to me.
